0:
log_level = "debug"

[download]
directory = "/photos"
# {library} keeps PrimarySync/SharedSync in separate trees so cross-library dupes don't collide+bloat (kei #559)
folder_structure = "{library}/%Y/%m/%d"

[filters]
libraries = ["all"]
albums = ["none"]

[photos]
# name-id7 gives every file a deterministic per-asset id7 stem so re-syncs reconstruct the same path and match existing files; name-size-dedup re-downloads recurring shared-library assets under new suffixes each cycle (kei #546), bloating /photos and self-colliding on content-hash .kei-tmp files
file_match_policy = "name-id7"

[watch]
interval = 3600

[notifications]
script = "/scripts/notify.sh"

[server]
bind = "0.0.0.0"
port = 9090

#!/bin/bash
# KEI_EVENT: 2fa_required | sync_started | sync_complete | sync_failed | session_expired
# KEI_MESSAGE: human-readable description
# KEI_ICLOUD_USERNAME: iCloud account
case "$KEI_EVENT" in
  sync_complete|sync_started) exit 0 ;;
esac

# Throttle: skip if same event+message was sent within 6 hours.
# State persists on the config PVC so pod restarts don't re-spam.
NOTIFY_DIR="${KEI_DATA_DIR:-/config}/.notify"
mkdir -p "$NOTIFY_DIR"
STATE_FILE="$NOTIFY_DIR/last_${KEI_EVENT}"
NOW=$(date +%s)
THROTTLE=21600
if [ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]; then
  LAST_TS=$(head -1 "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  LAST_MSG=$(tail -n +2 "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ $(( NOW - LAST_TS )) -lt $THROTTLE ] && [ "$LAST_MSG" = "$KEI_MESSAGE" ]; then
    exit 0
  fi
fi
printf '%s\n%s' "$NOW" "$KEI_MESSAGE" > "$STATE_FILE"

curl -s -X POST "$DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"content\": \"**kei** [\`$KEI_EVENT\`]: $KEI_MESSAGE (\`$KEI_ICLOUD_USERNAME\`)\"}"

targets:
  # Local gateway - used as health signal by the sidecar healthcheck
  - hosts:
      - 10.0.7.1             # OPNsense gateway
    interval: 1s
    network: ip4
    protocol: icmp
    size: 56
  
  # Public DNS Servers (IPv4)
  - hosts:
      - 1.1.1.1              # Cloudflare Primary
      - 1.0.0.1              # Cloudflare Secondary
      - 8.8.8.8              # Google Primary
      - 9.9.9.9              # Quad9 Primary
      # 149.112.112.112 is used for WAN2 gateway monitoring in OPNsense
    interval: 1s
    network: ip4
    protocol: icmp
    size: 56
  
  # Internet Services
  - hosts:
      - google.com
      - cnn.com
      - ghcr.io
    interval: 1s
    network: ip4
    protocol: icmp
    size: 56

METRICS_URL="http://localhost:9374/metrics"
HEALTHY_FILE="/tmp/smokeping-healthy"
prev_responses=""
gateway_was_down="false"
touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
while true; do
  sleep 30
  requests=$(wget -qO- "$METRICS_URL" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep 'smokeping_requests_total{host="10.0.7.1"' \
    | awk '{print $2}')
  responses=$(wget -qO- "$METRICS_URL" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep 'smokeping_response_duration_seconds_count{host="10.0.7.1"' \
    | awk '{print $2}')
  # If we can't scrape metrics at all, stay healthy (avoid restart loop)
  if [ -z "$requests" ] || [ -z "$responses" ]; then
    touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
    prev_responses=""
    gateway_was_down="false"
    continue
  fi
  # Detect gateway down: requests incrementing but responses frozen
  # (or responses equal requests means no loss, so down = responses frozen
  # while requests are ahead).
  # Simpler signal: if responses haven't changed since last check and
  # requests != responses, the gateway is not responding.
  if [ -n "$prev_responses" ] && [ "$responses" = "$prev_responses" ] && [ "$requests" != "$responses" ]; then
    gateway_was_down="true"
    touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
  elif [ "$gateway_was_down" = "true" ] && [ -n "$prev_responses" ] && [ "$responses" != "$prev_responses" ]; then
    # Gateway was down and responses are now incrementing again —
    # trigger a restart to recycle all raw ICMP sockets.
    rm -f "$HEALTHY_FILE"
    gateway_was_down="false"
  else
    touch "$HEALTHY_FILE"
  fi
  prev_responses="$responses"
done
